question: A 35-year-old man comes to the physician for evaluation of a neck mass and hoarseness. He has no history of major medical illness. Physical examination shows a 2.5-cm fixed, irregular thyroid nodule. His serum calcitonin concentration is elevated. The nodule is most likely comprised of cells that are embryologically derived from which of the following structures?
analysis: The elevated serum calcitonin concentration in the presence of a thyroid nodule suggests the possibility of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC). MTC arises from the parafollicular C cells of the thyroid gland, which are derived from the neural crest cells. The neural crest cells migrate to the ultimobranchial body, an embryological structure derived from the fourth branchial pouch. Therefore, the nodule is most likely comprised of cells that are embryologically derived from the fourth branchial pouch.
